passage: About 1,000 years ago, Cahokia, near present-day St. Louis, was the largest city in North America north of Mexico. Its central feature—Monks Mound, an earthen platform that covers about fourteen acres and rises roughly thirty ______ was built by hand from basketloads of soil carried by workers over many generations. Archaeologists estimate that between 10,000 and 20,000 people may have lived in the city at its height.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The information describing the central feature opens with a dash after "Its central feature," so it must close with a matching dash, even though it contains commas of its own. After the closing dash, the subject "Its central feature" connects to its verb "was built."
explanation.A: Correct. The second dash closes the pair around the extra information, so the subject connects to its verb "was built."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Without a closing dash, the extra information is never set off and runs into the verb "was built."
explanation.C: Incorrect. This comma could seem to continue the description, but extra information that opens with a dash must close with a dash.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "Its central feature" from its verb "was built."
